Convoluted

/kun-VAL-yuh-tid/ — stress on the second syllable · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something convoluted is tangled together in so many twists and steps that it becomes hard to follow or understand.

His convoluted directions sent us over three bridges to reach a house next door.

Worked Example

A detective must follow a murder suspect's trail: the suspect flew to three cities, used five aliases, made transfers through shell companies, and paid associates who each hid the money in different countries, each with a separate trick to retrieve it.

This web of overlapping steps, layers, and hidden twists is exactly what convoluted describes. The case isn't just hard (complicated) — it's twisted together in so many interlocking ways that following it feels like untangling a knot. Convoluted captures that sense of things wound together.

How Convoluted Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

complicated

complicated: having many parts, hard to manage

intricate

intricate: full of fine, carefully arranged detail

tangled

tangled: twisted together in a confused way

Antonyms

straightforward

straightforward: direct, simple, and easy to follow

lucid

lucid: expressed clearly and easily understood

How Strong Is It? — clear → complicated → impenetrable → convoluted

clear vs. convoluted

clear vs. convoluted: Clear is the opposite end of the scale from convoluted: a clear explanation follows one straight line, while a convoluted one twists through so many turns that listeners lose the thread.

complicated vs. convoluted

complicated vs. convoluted: Complicated is weaker than convoluted — complicated things simply have many parts, but convoluted things are so tangled and twisting that they become genuinely hard to follow.

impenetrable vs. convoluted

impenetrable vs. convoluted: Impenetrable is even stronger than convoluted: a convoluted argument can still be untangled with patient effort, while an impenetrable one cannot be understood at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — con-

Prefix — con-: together, with (Latin)

Root — volut

Root — volut: to roll (Latin volvere) (Latin)

Suffix — -ed

Suffix — -ed: past-participle adjective ending (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Con- ('together') + volut ('rolled') literally means 'rolled up together'; something convoluted is so twisted and coiled in on itself that it becomes hard to follow or understand.

Use the root in a new word: revolution

Use the root in a new word: revolution: A wheel's revolution — one full roll around — comes from the same Latin root volvere, 'to roll,' that makes a convoluted explanation one that rolls and twists back on itself.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Convoluted is stronger than 'complicated' — use it when a path, argument, or story has so many twists, layers, and turns that it becomes hard to follow. For something merely complex or intricate, the plainer words work better. Reserve convoluted for tangle, obscurity, and frustration.
